items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO HIGHER EDUCATION
COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the practice of registered pharmacy technician or certified pharmacy technician
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5584

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the practice of
registered pharmacy technician or certified pharmacy technician

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To protect the public by establishing requirements for registration
and certification of pharmacy technicians.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill adds two new sections to the education law.
Section 6803-a establishes the practice of a registered pharmacy
technician and the conditions under which an employee must be
registered as a pharmacy technician. Section 6803-b establishes the
practice of a certified pharmacy technician and the conditions under
which an employee must be certified as a pharmacy technician.

Section 2 of the bill adds two new sections to the education law.
Section 6805-a establishes the requirements for registration as
pharmacy technician, and section 6805-b establishes the requirements
for certification as a pharmacy technician.

Sections 3 of the bill adds a new section 6806-a to the education law.
This section established the circumstances under which certified
pharmacy technicians may receive a limited permit, and states that
students enrolled in a college of pharmacy are not required to be
registered or certified as pharmacy technicians.

Section 4 of the bill adds a new section 6809 to the education law.
This section establishes the special conditions under which registered
or certified pharmacy technicians may receive an exemption from the
requirements of sections 6805-a and 6805-b.

Section 5 of the bill would require the department of education and
the state board of pharmacy to consider an adjustment to the ratio of
certified and registered pharmacy technicians that may directly assist
a licensed pharmacist to dispense prescriptions. The department and
board will also reconsider the delegated duties, tasks, and functions
that may be performed by registered pharmacy technicians. Lastly, the
section establishes that registered and certified technicians must be
under the direct supervision of a licensed pharmacists, and that they
are not granted any independent authority.

Section 6 of the bill provides the effective date

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York is one of only four remaining states that do not require the
unlicensed persons who directly assist pharmacists to dispense
prescriptions to be registered with state authorities. This
legislation brings these individuals under the jurisdiction of the NYS
Education Department's Office of the Professions, including the Office
of Professional Discipline, and the State Board of Pharmacy.  The
registration and certification process described in the legislation
grants the Education Department the authority to evaluate educational
qualifications, verify that applicants are free from drug-related
criminal convictions, and, when necessary, investigate complaints that
involve pharmacy technicians. The legislation would allow the
Department to withdraw the registration or certification of a pharmacy
technician for good cause. For these reasons, this legislation
provides an additional and important level of public protection.

Current regulations allow a licensed pharmacist to be assisted by no
more than two unlicensed persons. Based on the qualifications outlined
in this legislation for registered and certified technicians, it is
reasonable that the department through the NYS Board of Pharmacy would
consider new regulations that would adjust the ratio and consider the
defined tasks that certified technicians are allowed to perform.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2008 A10177 referred to higher education
2009-10 A5379 referred to higher education
2011-12 A4605-A referred to higher education
2013-14 A4221-A referred to higher education
2015-16 A4841-A referred to higher education

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

None for local governments. State fiscal implications will be offset
by registration/certification fees.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law;
provided, however, that effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the
implementation of this act on its effective date are authorized and
directed to be made and completed on or before such effective date;
and provided further that the state education department shall,
effective immediately, be authorized to issue guidance and application
forms to, and to receive and consider applications from, persons
seeking to be registered or certified pursuant to this act.

summary: Establishes requirements for registered and certified pharmacy technicians; requires persons working in a pharmacy who directly assist licensed pharmacists to dispense prescriptions or have authority to add or to modify prescription records maintained in the pharmacy computer system to be registered or certified as a pharmacy technician.
